name: structural-scanner-design-decisions
body:
The structural scanner design:
1. Crate/binary: one crate src/structlib builds one binary structfrontend, absorbing src/mdlib; the md id survives through the stream id, so absorption avoids a second artifact (§4.1).
2. Config scope default: ON (all text formats graphed) — the everything-tracked-gets-a-File-node rule holds only with the default on; the include/exclude section narrows it.
3. Config shape: a dedicated scope section carries include/exclude globs plus a code_type, orthogonal to the existing types classification rules — overloading types conflates which files with what type.
4. Structure depth: minimal but useful — top-level keys/jobs/steps, tables/keys, elements, stages/instructions, sections/keys, targets/variables/includes, shell functions, Markdown headings — and stays free of a full parse tree.
5. CSV/TSV stays misc (§3 out of scope).
6. Dispatch: one binary serves all structural formats; the driver-injected lang_switch contract holds (a scanner emits zero lang_switch records itself), so the driver enumerates the structural stream ids.
7. code_type: Markdown keeps the built-in docs classification; the non-Markdown structural formats default to a config type, overridable via the config section.
